    Dwarven Stone¶

    [!INFO] Cut to the Stone — No Argument in the Forge The forge-true measure of Dwarves — every length a multiple of the standard quarry block, every weight a warm iron, every tolerance 0.02 mm or it jams.

    Base Units¶

    Cut in Dwarvengor from the First Stone — a 28 × 14 × 7 cm ashlar of deep granite, kept in the Guildhall at Stonehall. All Dwarven measures derive from it. The Coalsteel furnaces and Diamonds presses are calibrated to this block quarterly. Homunculi hobbers cut Romanium to it before it ran out — and now cut steel to the same.

    Domain Unit Relation Notes
    Length Grain base barley length — shared root
    Thumb 8 Grains dwarven thumb — broader than human
    Palm 4 Thumbs
    Stone-Foot 12 Thumbs 29.4 cm — shorter than Erisian Foot, deliberately
    Stone 28 cm the Stone — standard ashlar length. Also 1 × 0.5 Stone-Foot
    Rod 10 Stone surveyor's rod for mine galleries
    Chain 10 Rods 28 m — mine chain (100 links, each 1 Stone)
    Delve 100 Chains 2.8 km — a shift's haul distance. Dwarven mile
    Weight Grain base
    Lot 120 Grains small forge weight
    Mark 16 Lot 8 Ounces Erisian
    Pound 32 Lot 462 g — heavier than Erisian Pound (dwarven pride)
    Stone 14 Pounds 6.47 kg — for dwarves, for ore, for dwarves again
    Hundredweight 8 Stone 51.7 kg
    Ton 20 Hundredweight 1,034 kg — short ton by Erisian count, dwarves call it true
    Volume Noggin base 140 mL — one pull
    Pint 4 Noggin 0.56 L
    Stoup 2 Pints
    Gallon 8 Pints dwarven gallon 4.48 L — stamp-tested
    Anker 10 Gallons cask for mine water
    Tun 25 Anker vault cask
    Craft Tooth 2.12 mm gear-tooth pitch — see Kobre Gear-Tooth
    Karat 200 mg gem weight — same everywhere, dwarves assay hardest

    Forge test: a true Dwarven Pound weight rings when struck. A clipped one thuds. Every apprentice learns the sound before the weight.

    Who Uses¶

    All Dwarven peoples — Dwarvengor, Coalsteel, Diamonds, Cobal Kingdom (Marti), Romanium Dwarnov and Obsidian Dwarnov (South Erisdar), and the Eastern Dwarves communities on Erisdar. Also the standard for masons, smiths, and engineers across East Erisdar: if you want a bridge that does not fall, you hire a dwarf and you accept his Rod.

    The Homunculi Kingdom honors the Stone-Foot for tolerances but keeps the Gear-Tooth for micro-measure.

    Conversion Notes¶

    • To Erisian Standard: 1 Dwarven Stone-Foot = 0.965 Erisian Feet. 1 Dwarven Stone = 28 cm = 0.92 Erisian Feet — the source of endless stone vs. foot tavern bets. 1 Dwarven Pound = 1.022 Erisian Pounds — dwarven merchants round up.
    • To Kobre Gear-Tooth: 1 Stone = 132 Gear-Teeth (exact). Homunculi catalogue lists dwarven parts in Teeth; dwarves list homunculi parts in Stones. Both are correct; both claim priority.
    • To Vennerian Cable: 1 Delve = 15.1 Vennerian Cables. Dwarven surveyors mark tunnels in Chains; Vennerian pilots convert to Cables and complain.
    • Romanium: The lost Romanium standard was 1 Stone = 44,000 Grains of Romanium. Modern steel conversion is kept for nostalgia — every guildhall has a Romanium Stone of painted iron that weighs what Romanium would have.

    Flavor¶

    A dwarven measure is a promise. The mine foreman who says three Stone wide means three Stone, not two and a splash of mortar. Young dwarves memorize the Stone song — a chant of Thumb, Palm, Foot, Stone — before they memorize their clan. Elves call it stubborn; dwarves call it what keeps the mountain from falling on your head.

    At border markets with humans, the dwarven stall has two sets of weights — brass for show, iron for sale. The iron ones are heavier. Everyone knows. No one mentions it, because the dwarf will demonstrate the ring-test until you apologize.
